item.text: I’m organizing the tree around the next intervention to choose, with more specific alternatives beneath it—for example, replacing a checkpoint versus expanding an ensemble, or using raw scores versus ranks. Items that bundle several edits will be placed once under their main rationale; the notes will flag that ambiguity and the limits of noisy score evidence.

leaves={}

def D(key,name,question,desc,check,how,*children):

201 Multiple fine-tuned checkpoints from different model families are available, and the public evaluation set is very small (making single-submission comparisons noisy).
baseline 5
158 Preprocessing code exists but no training loop or cross-validation infrastructure has been built yet.
batch 12
402 Inference must be run over many checkpoints (e.g., multi-seed ensemble), so memory and speed matter. The task is regression with a continuous target.
blend 98
21 One prediction source is known to be substantially stronger than the other, so the blend will be heavily skewed. Without local validation of the blend, the leaderboard must be used as the oracle.
boosting 7
23 A high-level API is already producing predictions blended at very small weight into a strong baseline submission. The practitioner wants finer control (early stopping, iteration selection).
cache 17
156 A large multi-row-per-entity dataset requires both understanding (EDA) and efficient preprocessing before modeling. Full data is slow to iterate on.
calibrate 10
299 Ensemble predictions may have a small bias relative to the training target distribution. The test set is small and noisy, so aggressive bias correction risks overfitting to training statistics.
capacity 19
28 A gradient-boosted tree model with default leaf count is already producing competitive predictions that are blended with a strong external submission. The dataset is moderately large but the model's own contribution to the blend is small.
checkpoint 39
219 An existing multi-model ensemble already achieves a strong score. New checkpoints trained with a different data strategy are available but untested.
config 27
26 When experimenting by commenting/uncommenting code blocks to switch between configurations, it is easy to leave imports disabled, pass wrong arguments, or use the wrong prediction method, each costing a full run cycle.
cv_size 6
27 The model contributes a small fraction of the final blended prediction, so its individual overfitting has limited impact on the ensemble. A validation split reduces training data without providing actionable early-stopping benefit at such low blend weight.
debug 29
35 The pipeline has multiple expensive knobs (number of estimators, cross-validation folds, ensemble seeds) and the practitioner needs rapid feedback during development but full computation for submissions.
distribution 1
1008 A regression model outputs continuous predictions that must be discretized into ordinal labels. The evaluation metric is quadratic weighted kappa, which is sensitive to both per-sample accuracy and marginal distribution alignment. The target distribution is approximately known from training data.
domain_pretrain 2
19 The current best model uses a general-purpose pretrained backbone and has been extensively tuned on heads, image sizes, and post-processing with diminishing returns.
duration 6
63 After switching to a dropout-based boosting mode, the number of iterations must be tuned explicitly because the dropout mechanism makes early-stopping callbacks less reliable or inapplicable.
embeddings 29
218 A linear meta-learner already underperforms a simple weighted average due to small data. Adding more features increases the input dimensionality the meta-learner must fit.
external 3
872 A model has reached a competitive score and additional labeled examples are available but may contain noisy or ambiguous labels (e.g., low agreement among annotators).
feature_ablate 18
52 A gradient-boosted tree model is already performing well with a large engineered feature set, and the practitioner suspects some feature groups may add noise.
feature_cutoff 26
40 A tree-based model is trained on a large engineered feature set. A two-stage workflow is introduced: train once to measure feature importance, then retrain on only the top features. Validation scores (not public leaderboard) guide the choice.
feature_refresh 7
1087 A feature selection step was previously run and its output cached. New features have since been added to the pipeline, so the cached list is stale.
filter 10
435 An outlier list has been precomputed (e.g., via high-loss or distributional analysis) and the current pipeline is already well-tuned, so data cleaning is a plausible next lever.
filter_signal 4
840 Reducing the sampling rate and narrowing the bandpass filter saves computation but may discard informative high-frequency content. A prior best result used the higher rate and wider band.
folds 41
117 A k-fold training loop trains one model per fold but does not yet generate test predictions. The competition requires a single probability per entity.
fusion 5
646 An existing multi-branch network combines features from several input modalities through a shared classification head. A new branch trained on a different input representation is available.
group_cv 5
182 The raw data has multiple rows per entity (e.g., time-series of statements per customer), but the task requires one prediction per entity. A CV loop will split and train on this data.
group_post 11
256 A strong regression ensemble exists, and separately trained classification models that discretize the target into bins are also available. The idea is to use high-confidence discrete predictions to catch and fix outlier regression predictions.
image_size 9
1 An initial baseline uses a moderate resolution and a standard fold count. Increasing resolution improves per-model quality; adding more folds reduces variance. Both changes are cheap to test at inference time when pretrained fold checkpoints already exist.
inspect_data 1
154 Starting a new tabular competition or project with a large dataset where each entity has a variable number of time-ordered rows and many anonymised columns.
isolate 107
6 Multiple changes (input preprocessing and model architecture) were applied in a single submission, and the resulting score drop could not be attributed to either one.
learning 10
51 A lower learning rate requires proportionally more boosting rounds to reach the same effective model capacity. If the maximum number of rounds is not increased enough, early stopping will halt training before the model matches its previous performance.
load 26
301 An inference-only notebook loads pre-trained fine-tuned checkpoints and ensembles their predictions. Swapping the backbone size requires matching the hidden dimension in every downstream layer and ensuring the checkpoint weights were actually fine-tuned with the same architecture.
logit 3
634 Multiple models produce class probability distributions that are averaged with weights before submission. The evaluation metric is a divergence or log-based loss between predicted and target distributions.
match_preprocess 30
17 A new checkpoint was trained at a specific input resolution. Inference resolution should match training resolution for best feature extraction.
memory 24
37 The test set is large and predictions from many fold/seed models must be averaged. Materializing all predictions simultaneously risks exceeding available memory.
metric 15
47 The default loss or built-in metrics of the training library do not match the competition's evaluation metric, so early stopping and model selection may be suboptimal.
missing_scale 8
71 Gradient-boosted tree implementations can route missing values natively at each split. Mean-imputing aggregation-induced NaNs may destroy the informative signal that a group had too few observations to compute the statistic.
negative 2
22 During a blend-weight sweep, it is unclear whether the auxiliary source's residual information is positively or negatively correlated with the target after accounting for the primary source.
no_post 2
492 A pipeline includes both multiple blended models and a non-trivial post-processing transform (e.g., rank normalization or multi-stage calibration). The practitioner wants to simplify the pipeline but is unsure which components are load-bearing.
noise 66
34 A tree-based or other stochastic model pipeline produces slightly different predictions each run due to random seeds, data shuffling, or floating-point non-determinism. Before attributing small score changes to code edits, the baseline variance must be known.
nonlinear 3
1349 Multiple models are ensembled via weighted averaging of sigmoid outputs for a metric based on ranking (AUC). Raw sigmoid outputs may be poorly calibrated or overly concentrated near extremes.
objective 8
60 A gradient-boosted tree model is trained with the default binary classification loss, but the leaderboard metric is a non-standard combination of ranking and threshold-based measures.
output_bug 12
36 A gradient-boosted tree model is trained and predictions are saved directly. The competition expects probability outputs but the model may output raw scores (log-odds) by default depending on the prediction method used.
pipeline_bug 41
68 A data transformation is wrapped in a function, but the output has unexpected columns, shapes, or values, and the cause is not obvious from the error alone.
prune_member 104
200 An ensemble of two or more models holds the best score, and several individual checkpoints have been tried without matching it.
pseudo 3
813 An ensemble has reached a strong baseline score. Checkpoints from a semi-supervised (pseudo-label) training run are available for one model family in the ensemble.
rank 21
0 When ensembling multiple cross-validation folds of the same model architecture, the choice between averaging raw probabilities and averaging ranks can affect the final metric, but the direction of the effect may depend on other settings (number of folds, input resolution).
refactor 30
138 After many iterations, feature engineering code has stabilized and the same features can be precomputed and stored in an efficient columnar format. The in-notebook code is now redundant, slows execution, and makes further experimentation harder.
regularization 10
42 After a feature-selection sweep plateaued without clear gains, overfitting is suspected and regularization is the next lever to try.
replace_member 18
204 A mean ensemble's score degraded after adding a checkpoint that individually scored poorly. No per-member contribution analysis is available, only the overall score after each submission.
restore_member 14
245 A single strong backbone averaged over cross-validation folds underperforms a blend of multiple backbone families, because backbone diversity reduces correlated errors more than fold diversity alone.
revert 36
5 A post-processing step (e.g., converting predictions to ranks before averaging) has historically provided only marginal gains on the order of a small fraction of the total score range.
search 6
45 When tuning a single continuous parameter (e.g., a selection threshold) with all other settings held fixed, each run gives a validation score but no gradient information.
seeds 21
130 A single-seed cross-validation ensemble is already in place. Adding more seeds increases training time linearly but may reduce variance in predictions.
shift_cv 6
1120 A known subset of training data comes from a different source whose label distribution differs from the test distribution. Simply weighting those samples during training did not yield improvement.
signal_backend 1
871 The environment may have version mismatches or incomplete GPU library installations. The GPU library's internal API paths can change between versions, causing repeated import and type errors.
signal_features 19
678 A model has been trained with an optional auxiliary signal channel. The channel is plausibly informative but may also add noise if the model wasn't strongly trained on it or if the test distribution differs.
simple_head 2
9 A complex multi-head architecture with per-class heads and attention modules has reached diminishing returns. An alternative single shared-head design is available.
sparse_text 4
1079 A topic model with automatic topic count selection and remotely-loaded embedding models are used to create features for a gradient-boosted model. The pipeline runs but has not yet been submitted.
spectral 13
689 An inference pipeline using spectrogram-based features has reached a plateau. The spectral transform parameters (e.g., FFT window length) have not yet been tuned at inference time.
stack 33
98 A practitioner has serialized models from earlier experiments and a current cross-validation training loop producing fold-level predictions.
stochastic 8
358 Small training set with noisy labels makes the classification/regression head prone to overfitting, and single dropout masks introduce high variance in predictions.
stop 28
25 A gradient-boosted tree model is already blended with a strong existing submission and the model's contribution weight is small (1–2%). The model is not the primary driver of the final score.
strat_cv 4
127 The dataset has class imbalance and the competition metric differs from standard log-loss. Using random (non-stratified) folds and a generic loss for early stopping may not align training with the actual objective.
synthetic 11
221 A set of fold predictions produced with one data augmentation approach (pseudo-labeling) already scored worse than the best known ensemble. An alternative set of fold predictions from a different augmentation approach (input noise) is available.
target 11
426 A survival or ranking target is derived from a global statistical estimate (e.g., a cumulative hazard curve). The metric averages per-subgroup performance and penalizes variance across subgroups, so a globally computed target may under-fit minority subgroups whose event distributions differ.
temporal_features 9
70 A baseline with standard numeric aggregations (mean, std, min, max, last) already performs well. A date column has been excluded from aggregation because it is not natively numeric.
text_clean 9
413 A fine-tuned transformer is already performing well on a text regression task. The idea is to give the model a comparative anchor by encoding each sample as a pair with a constant reference text.
text_stats 14
388 A second-stage stacking ensemble already combines multiple fold/seed predictions from fine-tuned pretrained models and achieves a competitive score on a small, noisy dataset.
threshold 18
973 A regression model outputs continuous values that must be discretized into ordinal classes, and the evaluation metric (e.g., quadratic weighted kappa) is non-linear in the bin boundaries.
tta 25
647 The model processes a fixed-length temporal window extracted from a longer recording. Multiple overlapping or adjacent windows (e.g., left/center/right segments) are already available from preprocessing but only the center one is used at inference.
uniform 11
177 A k-fold ensemble uses per-fold weights (e.g., proportional to fold validation performance) to combine predictions. It is unclear whether the added complexity helps or just overfits to validation noise.
weights 7
38 A classification task with moderate class imbalance and a non-standard evaluation metric that combines ranking quality with recall at a fixed false-positive threshold. A fast debug mode (fewer folds, fewer seeds) is available for local evaluation.
window 9
643 A pipeline uses features from multiple overlapping or adjacent time windows around the labeled segment. It is unclear whether the flanking windows add signal or just add noise and compute cost.

 b.L('device','Align model and tensor devices','Place the model and every input on a supported common device and confirm library hardware support.','The failing call mixes devices or requests unavailable acceleration.','Inspect device attributes, accelerator availability, and the exact error at the failed model call.'),

for n,k in list(b.assign.items()):
 if k=='api_bug':
  s=' '.join(b.items[n]['general'].values()).lower()
  b.assign[n]='device' if any(w in s for w in ['device-','device ','gpu support','cpu execution','hardware-acceleration']) else ('dependencies' if any(w in s for w in ['import','file path','file-path','package','dependency','installed']) else 'api_contract')
replace_leaf('missing_scale','How should numeric input problems be handled?',[

 b.L('numeric','Adjust numeric representation','Compare scaling, rounding, outlier handling, or storage precision while keeping features and folds fixed.','Numeric range, resolution, or precision may suppress useful distinctions.','Inspect feature ranges, quantization, outliers, and the downstream learner sensitivity to scale.')])
for n,k in list(b.assign.items()):
 if k=='missing_scale':b.assign[n]='impute' if n in [71,167,173,548,565] else 'numeric'
# Modality ablation is different from adding a representation.
add('features','modality_ablate','Select input branches by ablation','Disable or restore one input modality at a time with compatible weights and compare against the full-input model.','Several trained input branches exist and one may add little or harmful information.','Inspect existing modality ablations and check that branch toggles have compatible model configurations.')
for n in [678,837,847,861,863,868,870,945,947]:b.assign[n]='modality_ablate'
# Update wording where the evidence includes retention rather than addition.
b.leaves['text_stats']['description']='Test structural, linguistic, or metadata statistics as an additional feature block and retain them only if they improve validation.'
b.leaves['signal_features']['description']='Construct one complementary raw-signal, spectral, derived-channel, or reshaped representation and evaluate it with a compatible trained branch.'
b.leaves['embeddings']['description']='Evaluate an aligned pretrained representation or auxiliary out-of-fold prediction block as features for a downstream learner.'

b.leaves['metric']['description']='Verify the exact task metric and direction locally and compare task-aligned versus surrogate early-stopping criteria when curves are unstable.'
b.leaves['blend']['_check']='Members differ in quality or residual patterns and the current blend has not been retuned after a component change.'
b.leaves['blend']['_how']='Inspect aligned saved predictions, standalone and blend results, and the change log; record whether evaluation comes from held-out data or only a small public set.'
b.leaves['blend']['description']='Compare fixed blend weights using aligned predictions, prefer held-out evaluation, and revalidate the weights after component changes.'
b.leaves['distribution']['_check']='Ordinal label frequencies are approximately known and the metric is sensitive to the marginal prediction distribution.'

b.leaves['distribution']['description']='Compare assigning ordered labels by target-frequency quantiles with ordinary per-sample threshold rounding.'
# Mark truly empty evidence, if any, explicitly rather than silently assigning it.
unassigned=[]
for n,item in enumerate(b.items):
 if not any(str(v).strip() for v in item.get('general',{}).values()):
  unassigned.append({'item':item['id'],'reason':'No reusable rationale is provided in the general fields.'});continue
 key=b.assign[n]
 assert key in b.leaves,(n,key)
 b.leaves[key]['items'].append(item['id'])

 'head':{'simple_head':{'attention_head':-.6},'attention_head':{'simple_head':-.3}},
 'combine':{'uniform':{'blend':-.5,'stack':-.5},'rank':{'logit':-.3},'stack':{'uniform':-.2}},

 'post':{'no_post':{'distribution':-.5,'group_post':-.5},'threshold':{'distribution':-.2}},
 'preprocess':{'match_preprocess':{'image_size':-.4,'spectral':-.4}},

}

extras={
 'combine':[
 ('The only evaluation feedback is a small public subset and many weights have already been tried.','Inspect public sample-count information and the number and spread of prior weight-search results.',{'uniform':.7,'blend':-.5,'stack':-.4}),
 ('Base predictions contain misaligned rows or inconsistent target direction.','Compare identifier order and held-out target correlations for every component.',{'blend':-.9,'rank':-.9,'stack':-.9,'logit':-.9})],
 'validation':[
 ('Related observations cross current train and validation boundaries.','Intersect entity or group identifiers across each split and inspect overlapping source windows.',{'group_cv':1,'strat_cv':-.7})],
 'replicas':[
 ('Repeated forward passes with the same weights and inputs are numerically identical.','Compare arrays from existing identical-input reruns and inspect evaluation mode.',{'stochastic':-.5,'seeds':.5}),
 ('Available fold checkpoints were trained with incompatible feature layouts.','Compare saved fold configurations and input schemas.',{'folds':-.8})],
 'examples':[
 ('A minority subgroup matches the expected test population and is currently underrepresented.','Compare source-group membership, input distributions, and known test metadata.',{'weights':.8,'filter':-.4}),
 ('A prior augmentation trial degraded validation without improving minority-group errors.','Inspect controlled augmented versus unaugmented validation and per-group residuals.',{'synthetic':-.7})],
 'post':[
 ('Group-specific thresholds were tuned on very few held-out samples.','Count validation examples per threshold group and inspect threshold variability across folds.',{'group_post':-.8,'threshold':.5})],
 'model':[
 ('The proposed weights were trained with a different input pipeline than the current one.','Compare training artifact configuration with the current preprocessing and tokenizer.',{'checkpoint':-.6,'backbone':-.4})],
 'selection':[
 ('The only feature importance ranking was computed on data used to evaluate the selected model.','Trace fold membership in feature selection and downstream validation.',{'feature_cutoff':-.4,'feature_refresh':.8})],
 'fit':[
 ('A lower learning rate was introduced without increasing the iteration budget.','Compare learning rate, maximum rounds, best iteration, and patience before and after the change.',{'duration':.9,'learning':.5,'capacity':-.3})],
 'features':[
 ('All model-derived training features were produced by models that saw their own target rows.','Match base-model training identifiers against identifiers of each stored prediction row.',{'embeddings':-.8})]
}
# Give the training discipline branch the same data-backed status as the rest of the action tree.
des={'nodes':{}}
def emit(n,id):
 n['id']=id
 if n['children']:
  bykey={c['_key']:f'{id}.{j}' for j,c in enumerate(n['children'],1)}
  checks=[]
  for c in n['children']:
   pushes={bykey[c['_key']]:.8}
   for other,w in contrasts.get(n['_key'],{}).get(c['_key'],{}).items():
    if other in bykey:pushes[bykey[other]]=w
   checks.append(dict(check=c['_check'],how=c['_how'],pushes=pushes))
  groups=[dict(under='WHAT FITS THIS CASE?',checks=checks)]
  if n['_key'] in extras:
   cs=[dict(check=ch,how=how,pushes={bykey[k]:v for k,v in p.items()}) for ch,how,p in extras[n['_key']]]
   groups.append(dict(under='WHAT DOES EXISTING EVIDENCE RULE OUT?',checks=cs))
  des['nodes'][id]={'groups':groups}
  for j,c in enumerate(n['children'],1):emit(c,f'{id}.{j}')
 else:
  assert n['items'],('empty leaf',n['_key'])
 return n
emit(root,'T')
root['unassigned']=unassigned

 for k in list(n):
  if k.startswith('_'):del n[k]
 for c in n['children']:clean(c)
clean(root)
Path('output').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
json.dump(root,open('output/tree.json','w'),ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)

def count(n):return sum(count(c) for c in n['children']) if n['children'] else len(n['items'])

No internet or external project information was used.'"','',
'The root chooses the next intervention; it is not a sequential workflow. Lower decisions choose competing repairs, representations, split designs, predictors, or aggregation strategies. A sweep or ablation is itself a concrete action when the trajectories do not establish one universally preferred setting. Multi-lever items are assigned once to their principal rationale; secondary levers are intentionally not duplicated. Operational fixes are retained when they enable correct predictions or reliable experiments. All items have a reusable rationale, so unassigned is empty.','',
'Uncertainty: many trials bundle changes, omit local validation, or depend on changing external checkpoints. Reported gains therefore do not establish causality. Items include unsuccessful probes and reversions; leaf membership is evidence of an action, not an endorsement of every conclusion. Checks use observable conditions and prior results, supplemented by prerequisites such as leak-free out-of-fold features and compatible checkpoint inputs. Push weights are qualitative routing preferences, not fitted probabilities or measured effect sizes. All nodes have data support; no prior-only action leaves were needed.','',
'Less sharply defined decisions: broad next-intervention choices are compatible over multiple iterations; member replacement versus checkpoint selection depends on whether the rationale concerns the full blend or one predictor. Validation fold count versus inference fold count, input representation versus model diversity, and calibration versus aggregation sometimes overlap. Recovery is separated from ablation by whether restoring a verified configuration is the main purpose. These are forced single placements, not claims that an item addresses only one lever.','',
'Items per top-level branch:','']
lines += [f'- {c[\"id\"]} {c[\"name\"]}: {count(c)}' for c in root['children']]
Path('output/notes.md').write_text('\\n'.join(lines)+'\\n')
print('Generated tree, desiderata, and notes.')

CONTEXT: Converting from GPU to CPU dataframes inside a per-entity loop is extremely slow due to repeated transfer overhead and per-row operations. 
ACTION: Convert the entire dataframe to CPU once before the loop rather than per group. Within each group, precompute the minimal slice needed (e.g., last N rows) and apply the transformation once, then extract per-column values from the precomputed result instead of recomputing per column.

CONTEXT: A single AutoML pipeline already ensembles multiple algorithm families internally. Removing one family and training it separately introduces a manual blend step that may not outperform the AutoML's own internal stacking. 
ACTION: Before committing, compare the OOF metric of the manual blend against the original single-pipeline OOF metric. If the manual blend does not improve OOF, do not submit—it likely means the AutoML's internal combination was already near-optimal for that algorithm mix. Reserve manual blending for genuinely diverse external models rather than subsets of the same AutoML.

INSTANCE: Performed a major refactor: disabled the existing Keras data generator, reorganized the feature pipeline to incorporate bandpass filtering, EEG montage features, and spectrogram features, switched validation to StratifiedGroupKFold with a custom metric, and restructured the OOF/inference flow. This recovered to LB 0.36, much better than the single-model 0.68 but not yet matching the best ensemble at 0.30.
1066 pipeline_bug 
CONTEXT: Adding a second model family to a blend degraded the leaderboard score, and the pipeline accumulated complexity (conditional paths, caching, mixed device settings) that makes debugging hard. 
ACTION: Strip the ensemble back to the single stronger model, simplify infrastructure, and simultaneously improve the cross-validation scheme (use stratified folds for imbalanced/ordinal targets) and align the training objective with the evaluation metric. Evaluate the cleaner pipeline before re-adding complexity. 
INSTANCE: Removed CatBoost entirely, simplified to LightGBM-only with forced GPU, replaced KFold with StratifiedKFold, added a custom QWK-aligned objective, and removed caching logic. The resulting simplified pipeline scored 0.81762, recovering most of the lost performance.
1112 objective 
CONTEXT: A custom loss function (gradient and Hessian) is used for a gradient-boosted tree model, and a large performance drop occurred that is disproportionate to the changes made to features or hyperparameters. 
ACTION: Audit the custom objective's gradient and Hessian computation for correctness. Ensure the Hessian is a proper second derivative rather than a placeholder (e.g., all ones). Remove unnecessary complexity like per-class weighting that can destabilize training. Move shared constants out of the function to avoid accidental redefinition. Test each simplification incrementally. 
INSTANCE: In v11, simplified post-processing (clip+round instead of distribution mapping) and added per-class weights to the custom QWK objective. In v12, removed the per-class weights, moved constants to module scope, corrected the gradient computation to be unweighted, and implemented a proper Hessian (replacing a placeholder of ones). This recovered and exceeded the previous best to LB 0.81929.
1247 embeddings 
CONTEXT: An existing pipeline with engineered features and gradient-boosted trees has a competitive score. The practitioner considers adding a large generative model's output as a new signal. 
ACTION: Before committing, treat this as a probe: submit the blended prediction and compare against the baseline. Autoregressive models prompted to output scores often produce noisy, poorly calibrated ordinal predictions that degrade ensemble quality. If the score drops substantially, pivot to extracting the model's internal embeddings (pooled hidden states) as dense features for the existing supervised pipeline rather than using generated text outputs. 
INSTANCE: Integrated a local Mistral checkpoint with PEFT/LoRA, ran inference on test essays to produce a 'mistral_score' column with parsing fallback, and prepared it for blending. The LB dropped sharply to 0.71784, a ~0.10 regression, indicating the LLM scores were harmful. The author abandoned this approach in the next version, switching to extracting embeddings instead.
1321 noise 
CONTEXT: Multiple checkpoints are available from different training runs and epochs, each with a recorded validation metric. The practitioner wants to pick the single best checkpoint for submission. 
ACTION: Submit a handful of checkpoints spanning different runs and epochs to calibrate the CV-to-LB correlation. Be aware that the checkpoint with the highest validation score may not win on the public test set due to distribution shift or overfitting to the validation fold. If the first checkpoint already leads, stop the sweep early rather than exhaustively testing all candidates. 
INSTANCE: Systematically swapped checkpoint filenames one at a time across 11 submissions, testing different runs and epochs. None of the 11 alternatives beat the original v3 score of 0.96040. The best alternative was run 2516 epoch 13 (the original). Higher CV scores (e.g., run 0318 CV 0.9650) did not translate to higher LB scores (LB 0.95917).
1324 noise 
CONTEXT: Multiple checkpoints have been evaluated, and the mapping from local validation to leaderboard has been inconsistent, possibly due to distribution shift or different preprocessing between training and test. 
ACTION: Track both validation and leaderboard scores across all submissions. When a checkpoint with notably higher validation still underperforms on the leaderboard, suspect a mismatch in preprocessing, augmentation, or data distribution rather than continuing to select checkpoints by validation alone. Investigate alignment of inference-time transforms with training-time transforms before further checkpoint searches. 
INSTANCE: Swapped to a checkpoint with CV 0.9662 (the highest seen). The resulting LB 0.95870 improved over the immediately prior submission (0.95388) but did not beat the overall best (0.96040), confirming that higher CV does not reliably predict higher LB when the architecture or preprocessing differs.
1332 noise 
CONTEXT: Several checkpoints from different training runs and folds are available, each with a recorded validation metric. 
ACTION: Submit a small number of checkpoints spanning the range of validation scores to verify monotonic alignment between validation and test metrics. If two checkpoints with the same validation score from independent runs yield nearly identical test scores, treat validation as a reliable proxy and reduce further leaderboard probing. 
INSTANCE: Compare leaderboard scores across checkpoints with different CV scores. The ordering was consistent: higher CV → higher LB. Two checkpoints with identical CV from different runs gave nearly identical LB scores (difference < 0.0001), confirming CV is a trustworthy signal for checkpoint selection.
1384 noise 
CONTEXT: An initial ensemble configuration improved the leaderboard score, but there is no local validation to guide checkpoint or weight selection—only leaderboard feedback. 
ACTION: Keep the first successful configuration as a baseline. Vary one factor at a time (checkpoint identity or blend weight, not both). If several variations all score worse, revert to the simplest blend (equal weights) with the member that had the highest cross-validation score during training. Avoid complex weighting schemes that are not validated locally. 
INSTANCE: Swept through 5 checkpoint/weight combinations (v23–v27), each scoring lower (0.963→0.959). Returned to ImageNet normalization and a simple equal-weight average with the best-CV checkpoint, recovering and slightly exceeding the original score at 0.96462. The lesson: higher local CV and simpler averaging won.
1480 restore_member 
CONTEXT: Adding a new, undertested model to an ensemble often degrades the combined score initially because the new model may be weaker or its outputs may not be well-calibrated relative to existing members. 
ACTION: First test the new model in isolation or alongside the full existing ensemble rather than replacing members. If the score drops, re-enable all previously validated ensemble members and use score-informed weighting (giving higher weight to historically stronger models) rather than equal averaging. Iterate the weights until the score at least matches the pre-addition baseline. 
INSTANCE: After adding the new models and seeing degraded scores in v99 and v100, the author re-enabled all previously proven ensemble members and switched from simple averaging to explicit score-based weighted blending (weights [0.24,0.28,0.24,0.24]) in v101, recovering to 0.27434 — close to the previous best.
